seahorse.name: Silverpond Armored Seahorse — canonical enemy
seahorse.anatomy: One upright seahorse with NO arms and NO legs. One long left-facing tubular snout, a curved neck, one pearl belly, one continuous curled tail, one blue gold-edged dorsal fin, gold cheek and chest armor, exactly two attached violet shoulder crystals. Preserve every canonical feature.

actions.idle: In-place looping idle: subtly breathe at the pearl belly, blink once, flutter the dorsal fin independently, lightly curl and uncurl only the tail tip. Keep the main tail coil and center fixed. Return near the initial pose. Do not attack.
actions.attack: One clear compact physical attack, with unchanged lighting and NO emitted effect. Begin in the canonical pose. Briefly bend the articulated neck backward in anticipation, then make ONE quick leftward jab with the rigid tubular snout, moving the head no farther than half the snout's own length. The neck bends naturally; the snout never stretches. Fold and reopen the existing dorsal fin slightly; only the tail tip counterbalances while the main tail coil remains fixed. Settle back near the starting stance and hold the follow-through. No arms or legs. Physical motion ONLY: no bubble, water, mist, spark, glow, flash, ray, aura, projectile, particle, trail, or appearing object. Existing crystals keep constant brightness. The full creature stays within the central safe area for the entire clip.
actions.defend: One-second hurt/defense: flinch the snout backward slightly at an imaginary impact from the left, close eyes briefly, recoil the head and armored torso together slightly, without rotating or deforming the armor independently, and tighten the continuous curled tail locally. Keep all armor and both shoulder crystals attached. Hold guarded stance; no new shield or limbs.
actions.defeat: One-second non-graphic defeat: relax angry eyes, lower the snout and gold armored chest gently, droop the dorsal fin and tail tip, dim violet energy while preserving both crystals and all armor. Let the eyelids gently close and hold the final drooping exhausted pose motionless for the final third of the clip. End in a still exhausted upright pose. Do not collapse beyond frame, vanish, explode or recover.

nautilus.name: Silverpond Rune Nautilus — canonical enemy
nautilus.anatomy: One nautilus with one complete ROUND spiral shell, exact gold spiral ridges and attached violet crystals. One turquoise face with pale pearl underside emerging from the left shell opening, one dominant visible eye and the tiny partially hidden far eye at the snout edge. Preserve five clearly exposed tentacle tips in their exact canonical arrangement; keep the partly occluded base beneath the face occluded and do not reveal or invent any additional tentacle. Never add limbs or expose a new eye. No arms, legs, fins or duplicate shell. Keep the round shell rigid and its spiral pattern unchanged.

actions.idle: In-place looping hovering idle: blink once, gently curl and uncurl the existing short tentacles independently, subtly pulse light inside the attached violet crystals. The complete round shell stays rigid, centered and fixed in size. Return near the starting pose. No translation or attack.
actions.attack: One clear compact physical tentacle attack, with unchanged lighting and NO emitted effect. Begin in the canonical pose. Curl the two forward existing short tentacles slightly toward the face in anticipation, then uncoil them together into ONE brisk short jab toward the left, stopping at their natural canonical reach. Articulate their curves without lengthening, duplicating, fusing or changing the number of tentacles. Other tentacles countercurl locally. The complete round shell stays rigid at the exact same center, angle and scale. Settle the tentacles back near the starting pose and hold. Physical motion ONLY: no light pulse, bubble, water, spark, glow, flash, beam, ray, aura, projectile, particle, trail, or appearing object. Existing crystals keep constant brightness. Preserve every complete tentacle tip inside the central safe area throughout.
actions.defend: One-second hurt/defense: briefly close the eyes and draw the turquoise face with its pearl underside and short tentacles partly into the existing shell opening at an imaginary left impact. The full rigid ROUND spiral shell remains at the same angle and location. Hold a guarded pose. No separate shield, shell rotation or new anatomy.
actions.defeat: One-second non-graphic defeat: soften the angry face, lower the short tentacles, dim violet energy while preserving every attached crystal and the exact gold spiral ridges. Keep the rigid round shell centered and fully visible. Let the eyelids gently close and hold the final drooping exhausted pose motionless for the final third of the clip. End in a still exhausted pose; no disappearance, cracking, explosion or recovery.
